yes: a paid order still waiting has not been shipped when the customer expects the goods, and nothing moves it but a person recording the shipment: no timer watches Paid orders and nothing in the application calls the ship endpoint (lifecycle L13, recovery stranded). yes: a checkout that reaches Ordering API and writes no order leaves the customer with no order and, on the web front end, an emptied basket and the orders page, so the customer is not told (lifecycle L01, recovery not created; WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:107-108; WebApp/Components/Pages/Checkout/Checkout.razor:111-116). A checkout that never reaches Ordering API fails in front of the customer and is not counted here; nor is an order call refused at authentication, which writes no command line (Ordering API's answers by status show it)

yes: a shipped order not delivered within the expected time leaves the customer without the goods they expect (the flow's promise to deliver the goods). The record this alert needs does not exist yet: the code records nothing after Shipped, so a per-order delivery confirmation must be added before it can fire. The bound is the customer's expected delivery time, which no source states and the code sets no time limit for (the customer's expectation of delivery, and the stage's own bounds). Its runbook entry has no tests, and that is the finding, not an omission: tests come from the failures of the move a stage's cases wait on, and these wait on delivery, which no part of the application carries out (step 13 has no lifecycle row; the code's last state is Shipped, Ordering.Domain/AggregatesModel/OrderAggregate/OrderStatus.cs:12). The stage's one recorded move, L14, tells webhook subscribers and does not move an order. Its cases go to the carrier, outside this runbook, until a delivery move and its record are added
